text:
yana: FYI I pushed allocator tweaks to reduce small-frag buildup (adaptive-slab-evictor). Observed a regresssion on kv-heavy prefill workloads — more OOMs and p99 jitter. Anyone seen this locally?

kevin: saw the rollout logs, curious if it's the slab split threshold change or the new background compaction delay. logs looked like space held by tiny KV slabs.

mira: can you paste the repro trace? is this on Dedicated w/ 80G or a smaller instance?

yana: Dedicated gtx-a100-80g pool. Repro with long-history chat traces (seq_len spikes). Quick summary from perf: peak GPU memory +18% on prefill path, decode peak unchanged. p99 latency +12ms on tail.

kevin: that screams prefill duplication — we keep separate prefill buffer + decode workspace for certain kernels. Did kernel selector flip to 'fused-attn' for short sequences? That can change workspace sizing.

siva: i dumped allocator histogram. Fragmentation ratio jumped to 0.34 (was 0.16). Most fragmentation in slab class 128-512KB where KV nodes live. Looks like we were over-allocating slab headers when prefill was holding many small cache entries.

mira: idea: enforce per-request KV cap (per_request_kv_cap) during prefill window to bound concurrent KV memory. Also consider turning on compact-on-idle sooner.

yana: tried setting per_request_kv_cap=64 on a test shard: OOMs stopped but latency increased slightly for long-context tails. throughput dropped ~3%.

kevin: expected tradeoff. Could we adaptively apply cap only when fragmentation > 0.25? e.g., dynamic_eviction_mode: frag_aware that flips behavior based on frag metric.

siva: we already emit frag_ratio to the allocator stats. Implementing a simple hysteresis should be cheap. But we need to be careful with bursty seq_len patterns — flipping too fast could oscillate batching heuristics.

mira: speaking of batching: when we throttle prefill we also change batching window. That explains some latency shifts — smaller batches cause kernel selector to pick less efficient path. Maybe coordinate prefill cap with batching heuristics so we don't fall into suboptimal kernel choices.

yana: good point. In the repro, when per_request_kv_cap applied, the runtime shrunk batch sizes for prefill requests (we route them to CPU-slow path more often). Need to keep kernel choice stable.

kevin: another angle: we can change eviction timing: instead of immediate on-prefill-append, do low-latency async eviction that frees whole contiguous segments to reduce fragmentation. "compact_then_free" vs single-item evict.

siva: compact_then_free is promising for reducing small-slab ROIs. But it's heavier CPU work — need to measure overhead. We should profile the background compaction CPU and memcopy costs.

mira: can we try a hybrid: prefill uses decode-first mode for entries > N bytes (avoid storing caches for huge keys), keep small entries cached aggressively. That reduces the number of small slab allocations.

yana: ran a micro-benchmark: decode-first for entries > 1.5KB reduced frag ratio by 30% and peak GPU mem by 10%, tail latency stable. Good signal.

kevin: nice. We should add a guard: if kernel_selector chooses a workspace-heavy kernel, prefer decode-first to avoid double allocation. That ties kernel selection and cache strategy together.

mira: Also, could we reserve a tiny workspace slab pool for decode that never gets fragmented? Like a soft-reserve per-device that handles KV decode temp buffers and is only used for short-lifetime buffers.

siva: implemented a soft_reserve before, but it reduced fragmentation only when reserve was sized correctly. If too large, wasted memory; too small, no benefit. We need an auto-size heuristic based on recent peak short-lived allocation percent.

yana: i can prototype: 1) frag-aware hysteresis to flip per_request_kv_cap 2) decode-first threshold tied to kernel selection 3) compact_then_free async path 4) auto-sized soft_reserve for decode workspace.

kevin: sounds good. prioritize (1) and (2) in a canary, since they're config-level and low-risk. (3) needs CPU benching and (4) needs telemetry plumbing.

mira: agree. Also add regression test: simulate 10k concurrent prefill entries with random sizes, verify frag_ratio < 0.25 and no OOMs at 0.95 quantile. Add perf counters: "prefill_dup_bytes", "decode_workspace_allocs", "frag_ratio".

siva: i'll add the allocator histogram exporter and an infra test that runs under perf harness. Also capturing a flamegraph of compaction thread.

deploy-bot: rollout v2.3.8-alloc-tune scheduled to canary pool #7 at 2026-03-16T02:00Z :rocket:

kevin: let's keep canary small. If canary looks good after 30m, widen to rest of Dedicated. Monitor alloc_frag_ratio and prefill_dup_bytes closely.

yana: PR incoming for frag-aware flag + per_request_kv_cap default to 128. I'll add notes to release doc and link the perf traces.

mira: thanks, team. If someone can run the micro-benchmark job on prod-like hardware (80G) and attach the flamegraph, that'll help finalize numbers.

siva: on it.

kevin: one last thought — make sure model-compiler kernel selection emits a tag in traces so we can correlate workspace path with spikes. Otherwise debugging the kernel selector -> allocator coupling gets hairy.

yana: will add tracer tags.

mira: awesome. follow-up thread once canary data is in. :thumbsup:
